verdict.rationale: Claude's own docs say incognito chats are never used to improve Claude, even when Model Improvement is enabled. The same docs refer to a Model Improvement privacy setting and to training happening when users 'allow us' to use their chats, which implies a user-controlled opt-in. Gmail, Drive and Calendar connector data is also explicitly excluded from training. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of where and how to turn off the Model Improvement setting and what its default is; independent or hands-on corroboration that opting out works.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can prevent my data from being used to train AI models

citations.quote: Your incognito chats are not used to improve Claude, even if you have enabled Model Improvement in your privacy settings.
When you allow us to use your chats or coding sessions to help improve Claude, we implement several layers of protection for your privacy.
We do not train our models on your Gmail, Drive, or Calendar connector data, ensuring your private information remains private.
